どちら が すき です か — Which do you prefer?
You compare two things (A は B より…), choose between two (どちら / ～の ほう が), say which is “the most” in a group (いちばん) and talk about the seasons and the weather.
side (“～の ほう が” = more…)
Which do you prefer, coffee or tea?
Of all the seasons, I like autumn best.
Today is much colder than yesterday.
To compare: A は B より ～ です (A is more… than B).
To ask “which of the two?”: A と B と、どちら が ～ です か.
To answer: A の ほう が ～ です.
To say the superlative: ～の なか で、X が いちばん ～ です.
To talk about the seasons and the weather.
When shall we go to Japan?
Mihai and Ana are planning their first trip to Japan. Yuki and Kenji help them choose the season and the cities.
Yuki, we want to go to Japan. Which is better, spring or autumn?
That’s hard to say. In spring the cherry blossoms are beautiful. But there are a great many people.
I prefer autumn. Autumn is cooler than spring, and the food is better too.
And summer? Because I have my longest holiday in summer.
Summer… it’s hotter and more humid than Madrid. And it rains a lot.
Then let’s forget summer! What about winter?
Winter is cold, but the snow in Hokkaido is wonderful. And it’s the best season for hot springs.
Hmm… Yuki, of all the seasons, which do you like best?
I like autumn best. Because Kyoto’s maples are the most beautiful in the world.
That settles it! Let’s go in autumn. Where should we stay longer, Tokyo or Kyoto?
Tokyo is lively and convenient. But Kyoto is quieter and has more old temples.
I want to go shopping in Tokyo too!
Then how about three days in Tokyo and five days in Kyoto?
Great! I want to go to Kenji’s house in Hiroshima too.
Of course! My wife’s cooking is much better than mine, you know.
and (A と B と = A or B)
ほう = “hoh”, with a long o. の ほう が = “no hoh ga”. Without the long o it sounds like a different word.
The stress falls on “ban”, and ん is a whole beat: i-chi-ba-n.
The first u in すずしい and in むし almost disappears: “s’zushii”, “m’shiatsui”.
1. The comparative: A は B より ～ です
In Japanese you DON’T change the adjective (there’s no “bigger”). You just put より (than) after the thing you’re comparing with:
The plane is faster than the train.
Literally: “Tokyo, compared with Madrid, is big”. より = “compared with”. ずっと = “much”: ずっと おおきい (much bigger).
The order is the reverse of English! English: “bigger THAN Madrid”. Japanese: “Madrid-THAN big” (マドリード より おおきい).
2. Which of the two? どちら … の ほう が
The question: A と B と、どちら が ～ です か. The answer: A の ほう が ～ です (“A’s side is more…”).
Which do you prefer, dogs or cats?
They can be combined: ねこ の ほう が いぬ より しずか です (Cats are quieter than dogs).
いちばん (literally “number one”) before the adjective = “the most”. You show the group with ～の なか で (among) or ～で (in):
The highest mountain in Japan is Fuji.
Who sings best in the club?
あつい, むしあつい (hot, sticky)
Your app changes its theme by itself according to the season. Now you can name them in Japanese!
あつい (hot weather) and あたたかい (pleasantly warm) aren’t the same. Spring is あたたかい; summer is あつい.
For objects: つめたい (cold to the touch) and あつい (hot). “The tea is hot” = おちゃ が あつい です. “The water is cold” = みず が つめたい です.
Everything you learned in chapter 7 works here too, in the past and the negative:
Tokyo isn’t as hot as Madrid.
Bonus: A は B ほど ～ない = “A isn’t as… as B”. ほど only appears with a negative.
“The train is slower than the plane.”
Answer to “コーヒー と おちゃ と、どちら が すき です か”:
Of the 4 seasons, which do you like best?
For 3+ things: どれ (or いつ for time).
Why can spring be a problem?
What’s summer like in Japan, according to Yuki?
Which season do they choose in the end?
How many days are they staying in Kyoto?
にほん の きせつ — The seasons of Japan
Yuki has prepared a short presentation on the Japanese seasons for Mihai and Ana.
Japan has four seasons. Every season is special.
Spring is from March to May. It’s pleasantly warm and the cherry trees blossom.
Everyone eats in the park, under the cherry trees. This is called “hanami”.
Summer is the hottest season. June is the month with the most rain.
But on summer nights there are fireworks. The fireworks are very beautiful.
Autumn is cooler than summer and the food is delicious. And the maples are beautiful.
Winter is cold. Hokkaido is much colder than Tokyo and it snows a lot.
I like autumn best. Which season do you like best?
What is beautiful on summer nights?
りょうり コンテスト — The cooking contest
Kenji came back from Hiroshima. And he asked Sofia:
“How was the restaurant?” “Very busy! The pizza was more popular than the ramen, you know.”
Kenji looked a little stung. “Then let’s have a contest!”
The club’s Friday became “the cooking contest”.
Three people are taking part: Kenji, Sofia and Mrs Suzuki.
Mrs Suzuki’s leg had already healed. “I’m taking part too! With a Japanese granny’s flavour.”
The judges: Mihai, Ana and Yuki.
Kenji made ramen. The broth took him ten hours.
Sofia made lasagne. It has lots of cheese in it.
Mrs Suzuki made nikujaga. It’s a simple dish of meat and potatoes.
“The ramen is hotter and spicier than the lasagne. The lasagne is sweeter and softer.”
“The nikujaga… tastes like my grandmother’s cooking in Romania.”
“Of the three, the lasagne is the best! Because I love cheese.”
Sofia said “Yes!”. Kenji looked a little sad.
Finally Yuki tasted. Yuki thought for a long time.
“Kenji’s ramen is better than the ramen at the famous places in Tokyo.”
“Why? It’s the simplest dish,” asked Mrs Suzuki.
“Because it tastes like home in Japan. It tastes the same as my mum’s nikujaga.”
Mihai voted for the nikujaga, Ana for the lasagne, Yuki for the nikujaga too…?
“Wait a minute! I haven’t chosen yet,” said Mihai.
“I… like all three. Both… no, they’re all in first place!”
Everyone laughed. “Mihai is the kindest judge!”
In the end, Mrs Suzuki won. The lasagne came second, the ramen third.
“Mrs Suzuki, please teach me how to make nikujaga next week.”
“In return, you teach me how to make ramen broth.”
That evening, Tama was the happiest of all. Because she ate lots of leftover cheese.
…Even though she was on a diet.
The following Friday, the club’s menu was ramen, lasagne and nikujaga. Everyone ate what they liked best.
taking part (“shutsujō suru” = to take part)
What was more popular at the restaurant while Kenji was away?
Why does Yuki like the nikujaga best?
It tastes like home, like her mother’s

Text to read: The club survey
Yuki did a survey in the club: “Which season do you like best?”
I asked the twelve club members.
Autumn is the most popular. Five people.
Next comes spring. Four people. Lots of people love the cherry blossoms.
Summer, two people. Carlos and Sofia. Because they like the sea.
Winter, only one person. Mihai. “Winter in Romania is even colder, so I’m used to it!”
Which season is the most popular?
Why isn’t Mihai cold in winter?
Winter in Romania is even colder
